simple.meaning: אַלְיָה (ʼalyâh) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “the stout part, i.e. the fat tail of the Oriental sheep.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 29:22. The surrounding context includes offering, sacrifice.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַלְיָה (H451) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.short: the stout part, i.e. the fat tail of the Oriental sheep
definitions.full: H451. alyah אַלְיָה noun feminine fat tail of sheep , still accounted a delicacy in the East; (Mishna id. אַלִּיתָא אַלְיְתָה, ᵑ7, , etc.; Arabic , compare Fl TWB i. 418 a ) Exod 29:22 ; Lev 3:9 ; 7:3 ; 8:25 (all || חֵ֫לֶב ); 9:19 , probably also 1Sam 9:24 for הֶעָלֶיהָ see Gei Dr (compare Tristr Nat. Hist. Bib. ch. vi Ri HWB Schafe Smith Dict. Bib. Sheep ).
